task: Make integration URL defaults deployment-configurable by fetching GET /v1/tools/configs at startup and replacing 15 hardcoded URL strings in settingsUIConfig.ts with dynUrl() closures (EPMCDME-10928)

component_scope.label: XL
component_scope.affected: appInfoStore, useInitialDataFetch hook, settingsUIConfig, settings utility, settingsUI types

technical_risk.label: M
technical_risk.risk_factors: New closure-based lazy evaluation pattern for defaultUrl (dynUrl factory); type widening of CredentialTypeConfig.defaultUrl from string to string|(() => string) requires all callers to handle the function case
technical_risk.mitigation: Fallback strings baked into every dynUrl() closure; fetchToolConfigs is non-fatal with silent catch; getSettingCredsURL explicitly handles both string and function defaultUrl via typeof check

key_reasoning.reason: Five components touched (appInfoStore, useInitialDataFetch, settingsUIConfig, settings.ts, settingsUI types) across Store, Startup-Hook, UI-Config, and Utility layers; bumped from L (4) to XL (5) because settingsUIConfig.ts is the master credential UI mapping consumed by all settings forms, and settings.ts is a shared utility used throughout the settings flow — both qualify as core shared utilities per the red flag rule
9 files changed (diffstat N=9 maps to L in the 7-10 bracket); 8 pre-existing files modified plus 1 new test file (src/store/__tests__/appInfo.test.ts), spanning 5 directories

Introduces a new dynUrl closure pattern (lazy evaluation of defaultUrl deferred to render time rather than module load time) with no prior precedent in the codebase; the type widening of CredentialTypeConfig.defaultUrl requires every caller of defaultUrl to check for function vs string; risk is well-contained by fallback strings and non-fatal error handling

red_flags_applied: Component Scope bumped from L (4) to XL (5): settingsUIConfig.ts (master credential UI map consumed by all settings forms) and settings.ts (shared settings utility) are core shared utilities — triggers the 'Touches core shared utilities' red flag
